items.title: Read the format first
items.body:
A resin label should identify the ingredient and format plainly, then show directions for that specific product.

Do not borrow a capsule study amount for resin. Different preparations are not interchangeable.
items.alt: Blank notebook, plain ingredient card, stainless spoon and clear glass on linen
items.evidence_label: Buyer check · read the product label

items.title: Studies test preparations
items.body:
Human studies tested specified shilajit preparations, not every resin sold online.

A study can inform a category question without proving this exact jar matches its material or outcome.

chart.title: What the study actually tested
chart.source: Pandit et al., Andrologia 2016, healthy men, 90 days.

items.evidence_label: Human study · Pandit et al., Andrologia 2016

items.title: One trial had one outcome
items.body:
A randomized trial in healthy men measured testosterone outcomes after repeated use of a specified purified preparation.

That result belongs to its preparation and outcome. It did not test this resin, general energy, or every buyer.

chart.title: One study, one defined question
chart.source: Pandit et al., Andrologia 2016, healthy men, 90 days.

items.evidence_label: Human RCT · Pandit et al., Andrologia 2016

items.title: Strength evidence is specific
items.body:
Another randomized trial studied recreationally active men during an eight-week protocol involving fatigue and muscular-strength outcomes.

Its preparation, dose, and participants were specific. It did not test this resin or prove a universal performance effect.

chart.title: Study scope, not a promise
chart.source: Keller et al., JISSN 2019, 63 men, eight weeks.

items.evidence_label: Human RCT · Keller et al., JISSN 2019

items.title: Narrow results stay narrow
items.body:
A human study explored skin-related biological signals after a defined shilajit preparation, not every outcome shoppers associate with the ingredient.

Keep each claim tied to the population, preparation, and measurement. A narrow result should stay narrow.
items.evidence: Human study · Journal of Medicinal Food 2019
items.alt: Neutral botanical leaves, magnifying glass and blank research card on linen
items.evidence_label: Human study · Das et al., Journal of Medicinal Food 2019

items.title: Ask about safety records
items.body:
A 2025 laboratory survey reported thallium in some raw shilajit and finished supplements.

That is a reason to ask about testing, not proof every jar is contaminated. The survey did not establish a safe serving for this resin.
items.alt: Blank analytical report, magnifying glass, graphite pencil and dark stone on a clean desk
items.evidence_label: Laboratory survey · Kamgar et al., BMC Chemistry 2025

items.title: A missed day changes routine
items.body:
The cited human protocols used repeated use over weeks or months. None tested taking shilajit now and then.

A missed day tells you about habit friction, not whether the ingredient works. Restart the routine without turning one gap into a verdict.
items.alt: Warm drink, stainless spoon, blank notebook and folded linen towel in a calm morning setup
items.evidence_label: Buyer checklist · match the format to your routine

bridge.title: Convenience is part of consistency
bridge.body:
A routine only works when preparation fits the habit. Resin adds a portioning and mixing step.

ShilaSource Himalayan Shilajit Resin is one resin-format option. Its label identifies ShilaSource, Himalayan Shilajit Resin, Dietary Supplement, and the other printed pack lines.

Taking medication or managing a health condition? Check with a qualified healthcare professional first.
